newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 19.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet approved the second wave of budget cuts this year, of 16.9 billion crowns. Further cabinet measures, which should save another three billion, must first be approved by parliament, bringing the total up to 45.5 billion crowns.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said yesterday in London that the EU summit in Amsterdam did not give any clear signals to the countries aspiring for membership. Klaus ended his visit to London yesterday, although he did not have the opportunity to meet with the new Labour leaders.

- State-owned Unipetrol is considering merging its fuel distribution companies Torol and K-Petrol under Benzina, which it also controls. Benzina would then gain 100 petrol stations, bringing its total to 400. The Anti-monopoly Office plans to investigate the case as soon as it becomes actual.

- President Vaclav Havel yesterday supported the reconstructed cabinet but said after separate meetings with parliament leaders of coalition parties and with opposition Social Democrats that the cabinet must have clear goals.
- At a general meeting of CEZ yesterday, the state, represented by the Industry and Trade Ministry will vote against paying dividends from last year.

- During the first quarter of this year, prices of supplies of products and services for agriculture increased year-on-year by 14.4 percent. According to the Czech Statistical Bureau, industrial prices increased by 18.l3 percent, which was the largest influence.
- The automotive industry federation (SAP) recommended the Transport and Communication Ministry to provide aid for buying only domestic and not imported vehicles.
- Yesterday, the cabinet approved a new construction law, making zoning and methods of construction easier.
- From today, Union Banka is decreasing fixed rates on seven-day accounts to 26.4 percent from 31.4.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - On Wednesday, the cabinet supported speeding up privatisation of large domestic banks, but it did not decide on methods or dates.
- Ceskomoravska Hypotecni Banka, the largest domestic mortgage bank, yesterday began offering mortgage credits again. It had stopped for several weeks, due to the chaos on the money market.
- Yesterday, the cabinet approved a proposal for the establishment of a Securities Commission. Parliament should begin discussing this issue in its July session.
- Plzensky Prazdroj and Becherovka have already appealed against the ruling from the Anti-monopoly Office to fine them, respectively, 1.5 million and one million crowns.
- During this year, German tyre maker Continental, which has a majority share in Czech tyre producer Barum, will move manufacturing from its factory in Dublin to Barum's Otrokovice domestic factory.
PRAVO - On Wednesday, the cabinet instructed Finance Minister Ivan Pilip that the proposal for the 1998 budget should have a surplus of 10 billion crowns.

- Nearly two thirds of those asked (65 percent) in a survey from IVVM, said that if parliamentary elections were held in June, the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) would win. Only 20 percent expected victory for the Civic Democratic Pary (ODS). The most favoured coalition (31 percent) was one made up of CSSD and Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL).
- The British brewery group Bass took control of Radegast brewery. Bass will announce this step at today's general meeting. It already holds a majority in Prague Breweries.
- On Wednesday, the cabinet did not approve proposals from the Industry and Trade Ministry for financial restructuring of Zetor Brno and Tatra Koprivnice.
- The central bank decreased its two-week repo rate to 25 percent from 29.
- The only domestic manufacturer to make it to the second round of the tender from CEZ for the supply of containers for spent nuclear waste is Skoda Plzen.

- CSOB bank increased interest rates yesterday for two-day, seven-day and two-week accounts to between 14 and 16 percent. IPB bank will decrease yearly interest rates for timed accounts for fixed periods of time by one to five percent today and timed accounts with termination deadlines and savings accounts by five to 8.5 percent. Foresbank also decreased rates.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Yesterday, the cabinet approved the proposal for new social laws from Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka concerning pension insurance and state aid for families. It will save 700 million crowns from the budget.

- State-owned insurer Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna did not succeed with its proposal to delay the new list of charges for medical operations. It is still uncertain how much money doctors will receive per point.
- Exports of pigs from the Czech Republic to the EU, which was stopped after pestilence was discovered in southern Moravia, could be renewed in two to three weeks.
- Last year, total exports from the Czech Republic to Vietnam amounted to $11.8 million, and imports were $17.9 million. This year, exports so far amount to $4.1 million and imports, $9.8 million.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
